title: Make Other People Come to You
summary: To hold power, you must force others to come to you rather than going to them, as going to others surrenders control of the situation. Forcing opponents onto your territory causes them tension, wears them out, and forces hasty errors, while giving you the advantage of preparation, home ground, and emotional control. True control comes from patience and strategic traps, whereas aggressiveness often leads to predictable and flawed decisions.
example: Talleyrand baited Napoleon by exploiting his desire for power, leading Napoleon into a hasty trap that resulted in his ultimate downfall.
Japan forced Russia to take an exhausting, long route during the Russo-Japanese War, giving Japan time to prepare and the home-ground advantage.
A stock market investor manipulating others into carrying out actions that serve his own interests.
A 'Beware of Pickpockets' sign that causes people to touch their pockets and reveal where their valuables are hidden.
An architect who allows competitors to exhaust themselves before stepping in to secure the project.
A hunter who uses a trap to kill a bear rather than risking his life by chasing the prey directly.
reversal: If an enemy is currently weak, biding your time may allow them the opportunity to recover and strengthen; in such cases, it is better to strike aggressively first while keeping control.
